driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

Every figure used is dated at or before the 2026-10-13 close; documents/live.json and news-log entries dated 14 October were NOT used.

newsLog.event: KOSPI plunges ~5-6% as Samsung, SK Hynix slide on China memory-chip progress; Nasdaq futures drop
newsLog.numbers: KOSPI -5% to -6%; Samsung and SK Hynix each ~-8% (5th straight losing session); Nasdaq-100 futures ~-0.6% to -0.8%; S&P 500 futures ~-0.1%
newsLog.reaction: The selloff followed Chinese memory maker CXMT's progress on a more efficient memory-cell design, with a server memory product targeted by end-2026. Memory and chip names are weighing on US tech futures, adding to AI-spending doubts after Broadcom's CEO called AI investing speculation 'a casino'

newsLog.event: Bank earnings: JPMorgan misses on EPS, Goldman profit jumps 29%, Wells Fargo beats
newsLog.numbers: JPM EPS $5.57 vs $5.90 est ($5.75 ex $658M securities losses); revenue $50.2B (+8%); profit $15.3B (+6%); Goldman profit +29% y/y, stock +4% pre-market; Dow futures up
newsLog.reaction: Goldman and Wells Fargo strength lifted Dow futures while the JPMorgan miss was limited by solid revenue growth. Also pre-market: UnitedHealth raised its 2026 profit outlook (+3%); J&J beat and raised guidance but fell on weak device sales. Dimon flagged large deficits and sticky inflation

newsLog.event: S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq close little changed as chip weakness offsets bank-earnings strength
newsLog.reaction: Indexes finished mixed/roughly flat: memory-chip weakness (Micron, Western Digital, Sandisk, Applied Materials, tied to South Korea's Kospi -6% overnight on China CXMT memory-tech progress) offset strength in bank and energy names (Goldman Sachs, refiners). Dow lagged on broader industrial/financial drag; yields eased slightly late in the day after Fed comments.

newsLog.event: NY Fed's Williams: one more 2026 rate hike still appropriate, none needed in 2027 as inflation cools
newsLog.reaction: Williams said he still sees one more hike this year as appropriate but doesn't expect further increases in 2027, with inflation seen slowing toward the Fed's 2% target. Comments gave a modest late-day lift to bonds and metals; markets now await September CPI (due Oct 14) for confirmation of the disinflation path.

newsLog.event: Oil firms as Paul Tudor Jones warns US-Iran standoff won't resolve before midterms
newsLog.reaction: Jones said the US-Iran conflict is unlikely to de-escalate before the November midterms, keeping a geopolitical premium in crude; markets also weighed new US diesel tax relief and the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel.
